title: Forest-to-shop flow chart template
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y3 lesson 8 (Forest-to-shop flow chart template (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 8: Rainforest products and trade. To understand how products from the rainforest are traded around the world

questions.q: Put in order: ship, farm, shop, factory.
questions.model: It starts where it grows: the farm. Then it is made into the product: factory. Then it travels: ship. Last we buy it: shop.

questions.q: Name a product made from cocoa.
Why is tapping rubber trees a good way to use the forest?
questions.a: The trees stay alive and can be tapped for years

questions.q: Core: Make a flow chart showing how cocoa beans become a chocolate bar in a UK shop.
questions.a: Cocoa farm in West Africa, beans dried, factory makes chocolate, ship or lorry, UK shop
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: box 1 'cocoa pods picked on a farm in Ghana', arrow, box 2 'beans dried in the sun'.

questions.q: Extend: Add one product from a rainforest that you use at home.
questions.a: For example: a banana, a rubber ball, chocolate

questions.q: Stretch: Why is fair trade important for the farmer?
questions.a: So the farmer earns enough to feed their family for the hard work they do

questions.q: Big question: how did a rainforest tree end up in your bicycle tyres?
questions.a: Sap from a rubber tree was collected, made into rubber in a factory and shipped to be made into tyres
